idiom_name: as-const flag registry with a keyof-typed lookup over process.env
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time safety to the plain mechanism: declare the flags in one object with as const so each value is a literal type, derive FlagKey = keyof typeof flags, and let the lookup helper accept only known keys - a misspelled or deleted flag becomes a compiler error instead of a silent false. Values still come from process.env (parsed at start-up) or from a provider; the OpenFeature server SDK (or a vendor SDK with generated types) is the standard route once flags are managed centrally, and vendor CLIs that regenerate the interface keep the types from drifting. The classic router object is justified only when the decision depends on request context rather than on a process-wide constant.
pitfalls: as const makes the registry read-only and its values literal types: a runtime flip has to go through a provider or an accessor, not through mutating the object.
process.env is untyped unless @types/node is configured, and a typo in a variable name yields undefined, which is falsy rather than an error - the flag silently reads as off.
In bundled front-end code the environment expression is inlined at build time, so a server-side flag read shared with the client silently becomes a build-time constant.
Generating types from a provider replaces one failure mode with another: a stale generated file compiles happily against a contract the provider no longer offers, so regenerate and typecheck in CI.
